compiled_state.description:
## Origin
Captured 2026-09-07 from the complexity-reduction session (session log 59a7-cb88-f2f9-4148) that ticketed the breaking-pass-4 epics. The operator asked what would have caught the complexity being removed, and whether the rebar-janitor skill can be modified or needs its premise revisited. This idea records the analysis and the proposed changes; nothing here is authorized for implementation until the idea is promoted.

## Finding 1: no gate asks whether the system is simpler afterward
The gates verify that a plan is grounded and self-consistent, not that it shrinks the system. Evidence from the criteria registry (`docs/plan-review-criteria-guide.md`) and gate history:
- Plan review (claim gate live 2026-06-23): A1 (over-engineering, NIH, config-surface proliferation) is the only complexity criterion and is ADVISORY. G6 approach soundness, E4 premise, G1G2 edit-set are blocking and catch grounding defects well (all four land-first stories of the breaking pass blocked in round 1 on premise/edit-set findings, correctly).
- LLM-Review code gate (2026-06-29): only `security` blocks; `deletion-impact`, `scope-intent`, `tests` are advisory.
- Module-size cap (2026-07-18) and complexity ratchet (2026-08-05) bound size and McCabe only. Mechanism ratchet (2026-09-01) blocks ADDING a mechanism and never checks that a retired one was REMOVED.
- Completion verifier checks the acceptance criteria as written; a cutover story whose criteria say "new path works" passes with the old path in place.

The removed complexity falls into five classes, each with a specific missing check:
1. Cutover residue (reconciler rollback toggles, HMAC after the op-cert cutover, the single-pass review demo, alias tombstones, `_engine_support/resolver` shim, `_call_with_retry`): no acceptance criterion ever said "old path deleted". Proposed: every toggle or `# mechanism-ok:` marker names its sunset ticket; verifying that ticket's completion fails deterministically while the marker still exists; T12 rollout overlay becomes blocking for toggles (no switch lands without its removal ticket).
2. Copies policed instead of collapsed (pydantic MCP mirror plus `check_mcp_models.py` 2026-08-07; MCP name-parity manifest 2026-09-01): a plan adding a check script that keeps two hand-maintained copies consistent must justify why the copy exists. Proposed: promote A1's NIH facet to blocking when the plan adds a `ci_gate` kind.
3. Gate-induced tests (four seam-guard modules written by module-size-cap split commits on 07-30, 08-13, 08-19; 88 held-out twins from the rebar-implement convention with no merge step; 30 modules re-running lint scripts over the real tree; CI-parity snapshot tests): no gate sees tests as complexity. Proposed: a test taxonomy in the code-review `tests` overlay (tests pinning refactor mechanics, re-export identity, LOC floors, import shape, or re-running a gate script are not behaviour tests and carry an expiry or do not land); a rebar-implement close phase that merges held-out twins; split-story acceptance criteria that demand behaviour tests, not mechanics tests.
4. Speculative or parked features (editor bundle shipped under a Proposed ADR; overlap detector switched off for performance three weeks after landing): proposed deterministic check that a Proposed ADR has no shipped artifacts; a config-disabled feature older than a set window opens a decision ticket.
5. Pre-gate structure (by-path package loading, 2026-06-08): predates every gate; paid once by the breaking pass.

Highest-leverage single change: a blocking net-mechanism criterion. A plan that adds a mechanism kind the ratchet counts must name the mechanism it retires or carry an A1 justification. The ratchet's docstring records the reason: 56 percent of sampled fixes added a mechanism.

## Finding 2: the janitor's objective and output contract produce mechanisms
The premise (a deliberate pause between features to buy back optionality) is sound. The skill (`examples/agent-skills/rebar-janitor/SKILL.md`) contradicts it in three architectural ways:
- The Phase 2 floor (validity 0.75, impact 0.5, reachable harm) selects for defects, not complexity. Defect remediation adds mechanism more often than not. The 2026-08-29 plan's 37 items were mostly additions (oracles, health commands, drift checks, metrics, pinning); the removals came from the operator's manual scope expansion.
- "Never edits code" turns tidying into ticket generation: 20 to 37 tickets per run into the same pipeline that produces the complexity, with no net-LOC or net-mechanism budget. Eight identical "Restore headroom under the 800-LOC cap" epics exist.
- Plans are approved against a frozen snapshot while main moves (08-29 approvals ran to 09-02; the dead-code validation recensused 98 commits later), so cites are stale by claim time.

What janitor remediation created that the breaking pass now deletes: RP-04's `REBAR_RECONCILER_WRITE_FACADE` switch, the eight `*_seam_clean_heldout.py` tests and the config-ownership gate; RP-03's `_call_with_retry` and `CREATE_ROUTE` toggle; the 08-06 run's MCP drift gate and the complexity-baseline CI lock (which now blocks the package move); the 08-29 run's alias tombstones (landed 09-04, deleted three days later), its rejection of shared MCP contracts (followed by the parity manifest on 09-01, deleted six days later), and its scanner-integration child, whose wholesale revert removed the mechanism-ok test contract and is the ancestor of bug amoeboid-amateur-guillemot. The comment-condensation sweep it seeded runs as about 1,700 per-file tasks whose commits invalidated cites in six breaking-pass stories and whose worktrees held the host's gate slots. Not the janitor: the duplicate-ticket incident (tier-2 replay harness) and the mechanism ratchet (Track I epic).

## Proposed changes to the janitor (modify, not discard)
Keep discovery, blind verification, prior-decision checking, and one-at-a-time approval. Change:
1. Split it into a tidying janitor whose only admissible outputs are deletions and collapses, judged by net LOC and non-positive mechanism delta at review, run between features; and a separate defect audit (the current skill), run less often and not called cleanup.
2. Cap a run at a handful of tickets, each landable in one session; measure the run by main's LOC and mechanism count a week later, not by tickets filed.
3. The janitor files no gates; a finding that wants a gate becomes an idea for the operator.
4. Discovery against a SHA, with approval and ticketization inside 24 hours or the plan is discarded.
5. No per-file mechanical sweeps; a condensation is one atomic change or is not done.
6. Held-out merging and seam-guard deletion move into rebar-implement's epic close.

## What promotion would need
A design pass turning Findings 1 and 2 into: the criterion text and registry entries for the net-mechanism and sunset checks (with red proofs against the breaking-pass tickets that would have blocked), the test-taxonomy overlay text, the rebar-implement close-phase change, and the janitor SKILL.md split with its per-run budget and success metric.
compiled_state.title: Make the gates and the janitor reduce complexity: net-mechanism criterion, sunset checks, test taxonomy, and a deletion-only janitor
